subject: Hosted API pricing qualification: expected monthly token volume & peak TPS
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhang <claire@finanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API pricing qualification: expected monthly token volume & peak TPS

Hi Claire [1]

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + a few follow-ups so we can put together a pricing sketch that matches your goals. Please confirm any of the numbers below or flag changes.

Recap from our discovery:
- Product: user-facing analytics assistant embedded in dashboard (text + some chart generation).
- Average tokens per API request (current): ~600 tokens
- Expected monthly token volume (near-term target): ~150M - 300M tokens/month (you mentioned ~200M as a working number)
- Peak TPS: you noted sustained spikes up to ~8 TPS during peak hours, with very short bursts up to ~25 TPS for <10 min during promos
- Unit economics target: you mentioned wanting to get to a target $/1M tokens [1] please tell us your target range so we can calibrate options
- Budget: you gave a ballpark budget range for hosted API spend [1] if you can confirm monthly budget range that will help us propose pay-as-you-go vs committed pricing

Questions / asks:
1) Can you confirm the expected steady-state monthly token volume (best single number) and the high-growth scenario (monthly) we should size for?
2) Can you confirm target $/1M tokens or a monthly budget range (e.g., $15k-$50k) that would be comfortable for the next 6 months?
3) Any hard SLOs for latency or required region (we logged US region during the call)?
4) I attached a small usage snapshot template [1] if you can populate with actual request counts by bucket (avg tokens/request, daily peak TPS) that would be ideal.

Next steps: once you confirm numbers above, Marissa (cc'ed) can do a quick infra/throughput check and we'll propose two options: (A) hosted pay-as-you-go pricing with volume tiers, (B) committed monthly with X% discount and optional Dedicated capacity if you prefer lower unit cost + guaranteed throughput.

Thanks [1] appreciate the clarity. Happy to hop on a 20-minute follow-up if that's easier.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.com | (415) 555-0118

From: Claire Zhang <claire@finanalytics.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing qualification: expected monthly token volume & peak TPS

Thanks Alex [1] really appreciate the clear recap. A few confirmations from our side: 

- Steady-state monthly tokens: we're planning to launch with ~200M tokens/month (this is our conservative estimate based on current users).
- High-growth scenario: with broader rollout and a couple of enterprise customers onboarded, we could see up to ~500M tokens/month within 6 months.
- Avg tokens/request: ~600 (same as you captured).
- Peak TPS: sustained peaks of ~8 TPS during business hours; during marketing promos we've seen very short bursts that could reach 20-25 TPS for up to 10 minutes [1] we need short-burst headroom.
- Budget: initial hosted budget target is $15k-$30k/month. Long-term (if we hit 500M/mo) we'd be flexible up to $50k/mo with a committed discount.
- Target unit economics: we'd like to see pricing in the $75-$150 per 1M tokens range to make the unit economics work for our customers.

I attached a CSV export of recent request counts (summarized). Let me know if you need a different breakdown. Happy to schedule a quick 20-min call with Marissa to validate TPS/caching questions.

Thanks,
Claire Zhang
Head of Product | FinAnalytics
claire@finanalytics.com

Attachments:
- finanalytics_usage_snapshot.csv

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhang <claire@finanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing qualification: expected monthly token volume & peak TPS

Claire [1] perfect, thanks for the clear numbers and for the CSV. That helps a lot. A couple quick notes and a ballpark pricing sketch so you have something to work with right away.

Ballpark economics (hosted API):
- If we assume $150 per 1M tokens (example hosted rate for our mid-tier gen model), 200M tokens/month => ~$30k/month.
- At your target $75-$150 per 1M tokens, monthly spend at 200M would be $15k-$30k; at 500M that becomes $37.5k-$75k.
- We offer committed/annual discounts and volume tiers that can materially reduce unit cost (eg. 10-25% off with 6-12 month commitments). Dedicated capacity can reduce unit costs further but typically requires a minimum monthly commit.

Throughput considerations:
- Sustained 8 TPS with short 20-25 TPS bursts looks fine for hosted API with appropriate autoscaling and burst allowance. Marissa will validate whether any additional concurrency or KV/prefix caching tweaks are recommended for your average request size.

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick technical sync (20 min) between Marissa + Claire to validate peak TPS behavior and caching opportunities [1] can you do Mon or Tue next week?
2) I'll prepare a short pricing sketch (pay-as-you-go vs 6-month commitment vs dedicated) once Marissa confirms throughput feasibility.
3) If you want, I can turn the numbers into a draft commercial proposal for internal review at FinAnalytics.

If your target is to stay under ~$30k/mo in the short term, we'll prioritize a pay-as-you-go + volume tiers sketch that aims for ~$100-$150 per 1M tokens, and show how a small commit could get you down to ~$75/1M.

Thanks [1] looping Marissa in for timing.

Best,
Alex

Hi Claire / Alex [1]

Quick technical notes from my side after a first pass on the CSV:
- With avg ~600 tokens/request and 200M tokens/month, you're looking at ~333k requests/day on average. That pattern is workable on hosted API.
- Short bursts to 25 TPS for sub-10-min windows are fine; we recommend configuring burst autoscaling policy + a KV prefix cache for repeated prompts which can shave tokens on common prompts.
- If you expect regular sustained growth toward 500M/mo, we should discuss Dedicated capacity [1] lowers unit cost and guarantees throughput for consistent heavy workloads.
